key_insight: BPP improves long-horizon robot imitation by automatically selecting a small set of informative past frames to condition the policy on, avoiding spurious correlations that arise when naively using the entire history.
problem_solved: Robotic policies often need long history to solve tasks (e.g., search or multi-step manipulation), but conditioning on full histories causes overfitting to incidental patterns and fails to generalize; BPP addresses how to use long context without spurious correlations.
method: Learn a lightweight key-frame selector that identifies a sparse subset of past observations (key history frames) relevant to the current decision.
Condition the imitation-learning policy only on the selected frames (plus current observation), reducing noise and spurious cues from irrelevant history.
Train end-to-end with objectives that encourage informative selection and robust downstream policy performance (e.g., imitation loss with selection sparsity/regularization).
impact: By focusing on a compact, informative context, BPP enables more reliable long-horizon behavior and better generalization for robot imitation tasks — making memory-aware policies practical and robust for real-world robotics.
visual_elements: Timeline of past observations with a few key frames highlighted (visualize selection vs. full-history conditioning)
Block diagram: key-frame selector feeding a policy network and producing actions
Bar/line chart comparing task success or generalization (BPP vs full-history vs current-only baselines)
Example task illustration (e.g., room search or multi-step manipulation) showing how selected frames resolve ambiguity
paper_title: BPP: Long-Context Robot Imitation Learning by Focusing on Key History Frames
paper_authors: Max Sobol Mark, Jacky Liang, Maria Attarian, Chuyuan Fu, Debidatta Dwibedi
